slots.label: Heading 1
slots.default: Available is not the same as backed up

slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: Both Microsoft and Google are explicit that they guarantee the availability of the service, not the recoverability of your content. Their job is that the platform is there; keeping a copy of what you put in it is yours. Deleted items sit in a recycle bin for a limited window and then go, and a compromised account that deletes deliberately can empty that bin too.

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: So part of managing a tenant is making sure something independent is holding a copy, and that somebody has actually restored from it. A backup nobody has tested is a belief rather than a control. We cover that with

Paragraph 6
slots.default: The rest is unglamorous and matters: multi-factor enforced rather than merely available, conditional access rules that fit how your team actually works, admin accounts separated from everyday accounts, and someone reading the alerts. That is the day-to-day of cloud management, and it is mostly invisible when it is being done properly.
